## Claims
- [proved] Conditional on the integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation, for
  \[
  a=\min(p,c)=1,\quad b=\min(i,j)=3,\quad p=q-i,\quad c=r-j,\quad d=ij,
  \]
  the truncated quotient is
  \[
  \bigoplus_{k=0}^{3}Q_{d+k}\cong
  \mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus
  \mathbb Z\bar x_2\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_3,
  \]
  where \(x_t=s_{((i+1)^t,i^{j-t})}\), and
  \[
  \bar y_1=-\bar x_1,\qquad \bar y_2=\bar x_2,\qquad
  \bar y_3=-\bar x_3,\quad y_t=s_{(i^j,t)}.
  \]
- [proved] The requested conditional \(a=1,b=3\) truncated target, including complete column and Pieri-row lists through degree \(d+3\) and unimodular complementary minors for both \(p=1\) and \(c=1\) boundaries, is established. No all-degree or parent minimality claim is made.

## Strategy
Put
\[
x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad
x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})},\quad x_3=s_{((i+1)^3,i^{j-3})}.
\]
The complete columns are as follows; delete a column precisely when its displayed condition fails:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{degree}&\text{columns}\\ \hline
d&x_0\\
d+1&x_1,\ y_1=s_{(i^j,1)}\\
d+2&
u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})}\ (p\ge2),\
x_2,\
z=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1)},\
y_2=s_{(i^j,2)},\
w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}\ (c\ge2)\\
d+3&
A_3=s_{(i+3,i^{j-1})}\ (p\ge3),\
A_{21}=s_{(i+2,i+1,i^{j-2})}\ (p\ge2),\
x_3,\\
& B_{21}=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1},1)}\ (p\ge2),\
B_{111}=s_{(i+1,i+1,i^{j-2},1)},\\
& C_{12}=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},2)},\
C_{111}=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1},1,1)}\ (c\ge2),\\
& y_3=s_{(i^j,3)},\
D_{21}=s_{(i^j,2,1)}\ (c\ge2),\
D_{111}=s_{(i^j,1,1,1)}\ (c\ge3).
\end{array}
\]

The complete row lattices are generated in degrees \(d+1,d+2,d+3\) by:
\[
h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,
\]
\[
h_2x_0=u+z+y_2,\quad
h_1x_1=u+x_2+z,\quad
h_1y_1=z+y_2+w,
\]
and
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
h_3x_0&=&A_3+B_{21}+C_{12}+y_3,\\
h_2x_1&=&A_3+A_{21}+B_{21}+B_{111}+C_{12},\\
h_2y_1&=&B_{21}+C_{12}+C_{111}+y_3+D_{21},\\
h_1u&=&A_3+A_{21}+B_{21},\\
h_1x_2&=&A_{21}+x_3+B_{111},\\
h_1z&=&B_{21}+B_{111}+C_{12}+C_{111},\\
h_1y_2&=&C_{12}+y_3+D_{21},\\
h_1w&=&C_{111}+D_{21}+D_{111}.
\end{array}
\]
Absent terms and rows with absent source columns are omitted.

Indeed \(i,j\ge3\) and \(p,c\ge1\), so \(q,r\ge4\). Thus, through degree \(3\),
\[
A_1=\mathbb Zh_1,\quad
A_2=\mathbb Zh_2+\mathbb Zh_1^2,\quad
A_3=\mathbb Zh_3+\mathbb Zh_2h_1+\mathbb Zh_1^3.
\]
The \(h_1^2\)- and \(h_1^3\)-multiples are generated by the displayed lower Pieri rows. Hence these lists generate every \((A_+J)_{d+t}\), \(1\le t\le3\).

For degree \(d+2\), retaining \(x_2\), complementary minors are:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{boundary}&\text{complementary columns and rows}&\det\\ \hline
p=c=1&(z,y_2);\ (h_2x_0,h_1x_1):
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}&-1\\
p=1,\ c\ge2&(z,y_2,w);\ (h_1x_1,h_2x_0,h_1y_1):
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}&1\\
c=1,\ p\ge2&(u,z,y_2);\ (h_2x_0,h_1x_1,h_1y_1):
\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}&1.
\end{array}
\]

For degree \(d+3\), retain \(x_3\). For \(p=1\), use:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
c&\text{complementary columns; selected rows}&\det\\ \hline
1&(B_{111},C_{12},y_3);\ (h_1x_2,h_2x_1,h_3x_0)&1\\
2&(B_{111},C_{12},C_{111},y_3,D_{21});\
(h_1x_2,h_2x_1,h_3x_0,h_1w,h_1y_2)&-1\\
\ge3&(B_{111},C_{12},C_{111},y_3,D_{21},D_{111});\
(h_1x_2,h_2x_1,h_3x_0,h_1y_2,h_1z,h_1w)&1.
\end{array}
\]
For \(c=1\), use:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
p&\text{complementary columns; selected rows}&\det\\ \hline
1&(B_{111},C_{12},y_3);\ (h_1x_2,h_2x_1,h_3x_0)&1\\
2&(A_{21},B_{21},B_{111},C_{12},y_3);\
(h_1u,h_1x_2,h_1z,h_1y_2,h_3x_0)&-1\\
\ge3&(A_3,A_{21},B_{21},B_{111},C_{12},y_3);\
(h_1u,h_1x_2,h_1z,h_1y_2,h_3x_0,h_2x_1)&1.
\end{array}
\]
The omitted displayed degree-\(d+3\) rows are integral combinations of the selected rows in each case; thus the minors complement the full Pieri row lattice, not merely a sublattice. Row reduction gives \(\bar y_3=-\bar x_3\).

## Gaps
- The proof is conditional on the stipulated integral box/Schur-basis description of \(J\), the integral Pieri rule, and the identification \(Q=J/A_+J\).
- Nothing here controls degrees \(>d+3\), proves an all-degree basis theorem, or proves minimality.

## Next
- An all-degree conclusion would require a separate graded-kernel or global elimination argument.
